precepts.text: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. The old leaven is sin.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

The old leaven is sin. Purge it out, that you may be a new lump. Because Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.

Christ was that unleavened bread that laid his life down for the children of Israel. So the passover and the feast of unleavened bread in Leviticus 23:5-6 both come to him: he is the lamb and he is the bread. With these the class counted three of the seven so far: the Sabbath, the passover, and the feast of unleavened bread.

precepts.text: Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: as a believer in Christ you must follow the steps of Christ. Christ came to bring peace; bitterness does not do that.
precepts.point: But with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth: meaning, I have got the bitter spirit; I have to talk to my brother in sincerity and truth. You have to go to your brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. What is the example that Christ left? Peter: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps”.

Christ suffered for us: that goes back to him being our Passover, sacrificed for us. And he left an example, so as believers in Christ we must follow his steps. Christ came to bring peace. Bitterness does not do that.

So we apply the scriptures. Purge out the old sin, the old man, that we may be a new lump, a new creature in Christ, following in the steps of Christ. “Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness”. That malice is the bitterness: a dumb thought jumps in, the seed gets planted, it gets nourished, and next thing you know you have malice, hatred toward your brother, and wickedness, because it leads to sin.

“but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth”. Meaning: I have the bitter spirit, so I have to go to my brother and talk to him in sincerity and truth. Brothers sweep under the floor mats and dump out the toaster at Passover, and there is not a grain of yeast in the house, while they carry an evil eye toward a brother or bitterness toward a wife. We are the temple of God; the leaven has to come out of the spirit.

And do not tuck it away for later, like the brother who puts the bread in the storage closet during the feast and brings it back when the season is over. Following Christ's steps means letting the bitterness go entirely.

precepts.text: For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. He died for our sins, so you do not have to kill a lamb and put blood over the doorpost so you do not die. You believe in Christ, you keep the commandments, we come together, we break bread and drink wine: you are under the new covenant.
precepts.point: He took the cup, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. That blood that we used to put on the doorpost represents Christ's blood: it represents the new covenant, Christ coming and dying for our sins. So do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

precepts.text: Purge out the old leaven that ye may be a new lump, for Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. To be a faithful steward you have to purge the old leaven out of yourself.
precepts.point: Let a man account of us as ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God. It is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.” In a steward you have to be found faithful. How?

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. If you want to be a minister of God, you have to purge out the old leaven. You cannot be moving with old leaven inside of you. Christ died for our sin, so we have to purge it out.

Paul says the same to the Corinthians again: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Then: “Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.” Cleanse yourself and you are new: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

That is the faithful steward: a man who has purged the old leaven out of himself, so that he does not live in hypocrisy, teaching the people to come out of the world while he himself does not live it.

precepts.text: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump; purge out the old leaven that ye may be a new lump, for Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. Leaven left among Israelites spreads and defiles others, so purge it from your spirit and from the congregations.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Christ likens the kingdom to leaven hid in three measures of meal “till the whole was leavened.” Leaven grows. Paul shows the other side of that same truth: “Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if you allow it to remain amongst other Israelites, that leaven is going to spread and defile others.

So the command is “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge out the leaven within our own spirits and within our various congregations. God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming, if you don't keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ was sacrificed for us, so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness and stop it.

precepts.text: That a man should have his father's wife is fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles.
precepts.point: The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.”

That is what Reuben did. He “went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard it.” Fornication such as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife.

precepts.text: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us; therefore let us keep the feast, with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
precepts.point: This day is a memorial, a feast to the Lord throughout your generations, kept by an ordinance for ever. It was not done away; even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, therefore let us keep the feast. The lamb of the Passover represents Christ, and the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
“ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.” For ever means it was not done away. Even in the New Testament the Passover is still kept: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.”

The lamb of the Passover represents Christ; Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. And the apostle's instruction is to keep the feast, not to spiritualize it away. “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” The memorial the Lord gave in Egypt, throughout your generations by an ordinance for ever, is the feast Paul tells us to keep, with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

precepts.text: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump; purge out the old leaven, for even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.
precepts.point: That is why the Levitical laws of sacrifice are no longer performed: the law had a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers thereunto perfect, for it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. We needed Christ, the ultimate sacrifice. Read verse 1 again with that understanding: the offerings went up without blemish because they were symbolic of Christ's coming.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” A little sin in the spirit will get worse. “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.”

That is the true resemblance of the Passover: purging out sin not one day a year but constantly, in prayer and fasting. “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ is our Passover, our lamb without blemish, and the peace offering without blemish in Leviticus 3 points to him.

precepts.text: What have I to do to judge them also that are without? them that are without God judgeth; the law is applied among the body, not the world.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The witness law was written when Israel was in its own kingdom and everyone lived by the law. Today it is applied among those in the body that understand the law, not to the world outside. Paul draws the line: not to keep company “if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.”

“For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? do not ye judge them that are within? But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.” The Most High judges them that are without, so the neighbor selling drugs on the corner is not your business; but when you see sin among Israel, do not hide it, bring it out, send it up to the leadership or correct it yourself.

precepts.text: Fornication that one should have his father's wife; the law of Leviticus 18:8 was being broken in the days of the apostles.
precepts.point: This very sin was reported among the Corinthians, a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife. The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
“The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.” That is the stepmother. The wicked mind reasons that she is not the biological mother, so it is fine to lust after her; the scripture says no, that is wicked.

This very sin was reported among the Corinthians: “It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.” The law had already forbidden it, and it was being done in Egypt and Canaan; that is why the Most High opened the chapter the way He did, and why it was still being broken in the days of the apostles.

precepts.text: Doing worse than the heathen is the same rebuke Paul gives, fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles found among the people.
precepts.point: He sets a carved idol in the house of God, the very house of which the Most High said to David and Solomon, In this house and in Jerusalem will I put my name for ever, and Manasseh makes Judah do worse than the heathen the Lord destroyed before them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.” Doing worse than the heathen is the same rebuke Paul gives: a sin found among the people that is not so much as named among the Gentiles.

That is Manasseh. He set “a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God”, the very house of which God said to David and Solomon, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever”. “So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.”

We must be sincere: we believe Christ is coming back with vengeance, we believe we are the people of this book, even though we are a small remnant and the whole world is pushing the lie.
